info.name: Huntress API Reference Accounts Signals API

params.name: limit
params.description: Max number of resources returned in a paged collection. Defaults to 10, with a minimum of 1 and maximum 500.

params.name: page_token
params.description: Token used to request the next page in paginated results. Defaults to 'null'

params.name: sort_field
params.description: Field to sort by. Defaults to 'id'.

params.name: investigated_at_min
params.description: Filter by an ISO-8601 formatted date string that represents the lower bound of the search range for the investigated_at date.

params.name: investigated_at_max
params.description: Filter by an ISO-8601 formatted date string that represents the upper bound of the search range for the investigated_at date.

params.name: entity_type
params.description: Filter by the entity type that the Signal originated from. This filter can be used without specifying entity_id.

params.name: entity_id
params.description: Filter by the entity ID that the Signal originated from. Must be used in tandem with entity_type parameter.

params.name: organization_id
params.description: Filter by organization ID within Huntress account

params.name: types
params.description: Filter by the types of Signal, must be comma-separated string containing the values: `Antivirus, Process Insights, Managed ITDR, Footholds, MDE Detections, SIEM, Ransomware Canaries, Favicon Detections, Attack Disruptions, App Control`

params.name: statuses
params.description: Filter by status. Must be comma-separated string containing the values: `reported`, `closed`

items.docs:
Shows details of Signals belonging to the account associated with your API credentials.

Signals are used to highlight interesting user or system behaviors that an analyst can reference during a cyber investigation.
A detected Signal could be as broad and low fidelity as the detection of a command line user running whoami, or it could be as specific and high fidelity as detecting a known malware file.

**Note:** This endpoint will also return a `pagination` key on the root level.
